body:
alex_connor: Quick ping — we need a pragmatic hedging + fairshare strategy for upcoming Q3/Q4 reservations across NA/EU/APAC. Forecasts show a surge risk and vendors are giving variable lead times. Can we sketch options here?

maya_patel: +1. Put a few baseline numbers: our current baseline is ~120k GPU-hours/month (mixed). Peak months projection (holiday/marketing pushes) ~165k GPU-hours/mo. So plan for ~38% peak growth.

samuel_ng: Do we have vendor lead times lined up? I checked two suppliers: H200 quoting 10–14 weeks; H100 6–10 weeks but limited batches; L40S 3–6 weeks and easier to get. These are regional — APAC lead times longer by ~20%.

leah_wong: TL;DR: hedge across model classes and regions. Tactical idea: reserve a smaller committed pool in every region for latency-critical traffic, keep a centralized burst pool (NA) for throughput, and rely on L40S for batched workloads.

alex_connor: Rough cost/efficiency tradeoffs? We need numbers for booking decisions.

maya_patel: Back-of-envelope hourly cost (rack rate, incl infra overhead): H200 ~ $6.50/hr, H100 ~ $4.75/hr, L40S ~ $2.80/hr. (These are supplier quotes + ops buffer). Also factor utilization: reserved capacity amortizes only if >70% utilized.

samuel_ng: For workload mapping: embeddings and batch rerankers -> L40S (good perf/cost). Chat+low-latency -> H200 preferred. Large-context offline evals -> H100 is cost-effective if we can get enough units.

leah_wong: Proposed allocation pattern (initial):
- Region reserved slice: 50% of critical baseline (keeps SLAs)
- Centralized burst (cross-region failover): 30% committed in NA + autoscale to on-demand for spikes
- Spot / short-term on-demand: 20% flexible for experimental workloads
This is a starting hedge; we can tune per-team fairshare.

alex_connor: I like that. How do we implement fairshare routing? We can't saturate a region with a single customer's traffic.

maya_patel: We should add weights into the routing layer: route_priority = {reserved_region: 0.8, burst_pool: 0.15, spot: 0.05} then per-customer caps. We already have route policies per model in the control plane. Example config snippet: 

```
reserve_policy:
  region: eu-west-1
  model_class: h200
  min_capacity_gpus: 20
  hedge_ratio: 0.25
  fairshare_caps:
    teamA: 0.4
    teamB: 0.3
    infra: 0.3
```

samuel_ng: One operational caveat: vendor windows overlap — you might lock up H100 inventory and miss H200 deliveries. Suggest staging purchase orders spaced by 2–3 weeks to smooth lead-time cliffs. Also escalate APAC orders earlier.

leah_wong: Agree. Also recommend a small tactical buffer (10–15%) of reserve capacity specifically for critical customers during marketing pushes — funded from committed pool to avoid overrun charges.

infra-bot: :warning: Reminder: reservation window for Vendor X opens in 48h for H200 allocations. Current cart: H200 x 40 units (requested by infra). Please confirm by EOD.

alex_connor: Thanks infra-bot. Decision: keep H200 cart at 40 for NA, reduce EU to 18, and add L40S 50 units across EU/APAC for batch. That keeps global buffer ~12%.

maya_patel: I'll update the cost model and run utilization scenarios: baseline/peak/stress (100/120/150% of peak). Will share a spreadsheet.

samuel_ng: I'll sequence PO windows and confirm lead times with vendor contacts. Also will add contingency clause for partial ship.

leah_wong: I'll draft router policy changes and per-team fairshare caps. Plan a 30-min sync tomorrow to finalize numbers and owners.

alex_connor: Action items:
- maya: updated cost + utilization scenarios (due 24h)
- samuel: finalize PO schedule + vendor confirmation (48h)
- leah: router policy PR + fairshare caps draft (48h)
- infra-bot: reminder 24h before checkout window

alex_connor: Thanks everyone. If anything changes on vendor windows ping here — otherwise we meet tomorrow. :thumbsup:
